one_line: A 23-second continuous POV walk through a mall behind a bassinet stroller with a baby inside, where typewriter text tells parents that choosing a bassinet over an infant car-seat stroller ('Donna') is a huge service to development, then asks them to send it to a parent who must know, closing on the physiotherapist's logo card.

hook.visual: Handheld POV from behind a grey bassinet stroller in a bright mall corridor, baby lying face down inside, escalators and shoppers ahead. No cut for the first ~20 s. First frame (0.0 s) has no text; the first text line lands by 1.5 s.
hook.on_screen_text: בכל פעם שתבחרו לקחת את התינוק שלכם בעגלת אמבטיה ולא בעגלת דונה (Every time you choose to take your baby in a bassinet stroller and not a Donna stroller), then "תדעו שאתם" (know that you) and a neon starburst sticker "שירות אדיר להתפתחות!" (a huge service to development!)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: it states a daily gear choice parents are making right now (bassinet vs Donna) and promises a developmental benefit within 3 s, with a visible real baby and a real mall as proof of an in-the-wild moment. The neon starburst on the key promise (6.0 to 7.5 s) is the loudest visual element.

payoff: The reason arrives at 12 to 15 s (the bassinet allows freedom of movement), the risk claim at 16.5 to 19 s (prolonged Donna use and head flattening, a creator claim not shown in the video), the share ask at 19.5 s and the brand card at 21 s.
cta: Explicit share ask at 19.5 s: 'Pass it to the parent who must know this' (the caption repeats it), then a logo card; no follow or link ask on screen.
share_or_comment_trigger: A concrete either/or choice many parents make daily, framed as protecting the baby's development, plus an explicit instruction to send it to a parent who needs to know. 149 comments and a caption callback to an earlier post suggest a returning audience (inferred).
why_it_worked: 271,434 views against an account median of 6,915 (39.3x): a single clear A vs B parenting choice that a parent can forward in one tap, with a spoken-free format that works muted.

like_rate 0.74% (2,007 likes) with 149 comments is above the 0.3% paid flag, so the reach looks earned; the explicit 'send to a parent who must know' line at 19.5 s targets shares (share count not provided in meta).
Expert credibility is built in: account name and end card state developmental physiotherapy, and the caption adds a mall anecdote and a medical-advice disclaimer.
paid_signal: no: like_rate 0.74% is above the 0.3% threshold and 149 comments is healthy for the view count, so the pattern does not look like paid boosting.

solo_route.how: 1) Get a barter developmental physio or OT to give you one claim they will stand behind, as 3 short lines (the choice, the reason, the risk) plus a not-medical-advice line for the caption. 2) Film or generate 20 s of single-take stroller POV: your own stroller walk with a plush, or an AI image-to-video clip of a stroller POV in a mall, or a friend's baby only with the parent's written consent. 3) In CapCut use the typewriter text animation in plain white, one neon starburst sticker on the single promise phrase, four text screens, then 'send this to a parent who needs to know'. 4) End with a 2 s white card with the LumeBook logo plus the expert's name and title.
solo_route.needs: A barter expert who owns the claim (LumeBook should not make medical claims itself); consent if any real baby is filmed; label any AI footage as illustration.

lumebook_version.hook_he: הבחירה הקטנה הזו משפיעה על ההתפתחות של התינוק
lumebook_version.concept: A barter developmental physio gives one everyday-gear do/don't (for example tummy time moments or carrier time) as typewriter text over a single POV b-roll walk, ending with 'send it to a parent who needs to know' and a LumeBook plus expert end card.

evidence_notes: Observed: all on-screen Hebrew, the single continuous take, CapCut watermark, starburst sticker, the end card. Spoken: whisper returned one cue 'תודה רבה' (thank you very much) spanning 0 to 22.96 s, almost certainly a hallucination over music or silence, so there is no usable speech transcript and all narration is on-screen text. Inferred: typewriter reveal (partial words at 10.5 s and 12.0 s), that the text completions at 10.5 s ('אב') and 18.0 s ('להשטח') follow the caption, that 'Donna' means an infant car-seat carrier (the caption calls it a 'סל קל'), and the paid-signal read. The verb between 'שאתם' and 'שירות' was not visible in sampled frames. Medical claims come from the creator and are not proven by the video. meta.json duration_s is null; frames/index.json gives 22.98 s.
